---
title: Home
---

This example demonstrates the **navbar** and **page-footer** —
two pieces of per-document chrome that live at the top level of
metadata (not under `website.`), so they work the same whether
the document stands alone or sits inside a multi-page project.

The navbar at the top of this page has:

- A **brand label** ("Demo Site") that falls through
  `navbar.title → website.title → document.title`. The first
  non-empty wins; `website.title` is the next fallback if you
  remove `navbar.title:`.
- Three **left-side items**: Home, About, and a Tools dropdown.
- One **right-side item**: a GitHub icon link to an external URL.
- An **active highlight** on the currently-rendered page.

The page-footer at the bottom has three regions (left / center /
right). Footer items pointing at `.qmd` source paths are rewritten
to `.html`. Footer items don't get an active highlight — they're
static cross-site chrome.

See the [About](about.qmd) page or open the
[Tools dropdown](tools/index.qmd).
